text.p1: Christmas is a special time. Every year, we celebrate the birth of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ. After the fall of Adam and Eve, the people of God were waiting for the Messiah, the chosen one, who would become the king of Israel and lead them. For many years, God prepared His faithful to welcome the Messiah, and one night, in a place called Bethlehem, the promised one, Christ was born.
text.p2: The whole story of the Old Testament is about preparation to meet Jesus. The narratives of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph tell us something about Christ. On this website, you can prepare to meet baby Jesus on the day of His birth.

Christ is the Creator of the World.id: Christ is the Creator of the World

Creation of the World.verse: Then God saw everything that He had made, and indeed it was very good. So the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
Creation of the World.text: In the beginning, God created everything! The picture shows the world right after God made it. Do you see the big, yellow sun? It came into being by the power of God’s words and filled the whole world with light. Beside the sun, you can see our Earth. On the Earth, there is a big tree with a fish swimming in the water, a bird flying in the sky, and an animal standing on the ground. it seems like the artist forgot something in this picture! What do you think the artist should have drawn? Probably, people. But the thing is that people didn't exist yet! God created people later.

The Very First People.verse: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
The Very First People.text: The painting depicts Adam and Eve. Do you see the figures of a man and a woman? They are the first humans. In the painting, Adam and Eve are gazing at each other in astonishment. Their hands seem to reach out towards one another. The artist has attempted to capture the moment when two humans first laid eyes on each other. What do you think the first humans might have been thinking? Everything must have been so new and wondrous for them.

Cast Out of Paradise.verse: So He drove out the man; and He placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Cast Out of Paradise.text: In the scene of the expulsion from paradise, the artist depicted a snake looking at Adam and Eve. The snake looks kind of mean, doesn’t it? Adam is covering his face with his hand. He looks sad. It’s like he knows he made a big mistake. Eve is holding an apple and looking up, scared. Who do you think the artist painted with a flaming sword at the top of the picture? It’s the flaming sword that will now keep people from going back to the garden.

Christ is Our Savior Who Sacrificed Hims.id: Christ is Our Savior Who Sacrificed Himself for Us

Jacob's Ladder.verse: So he came to a certain place and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it at his head, and he lay down in that place to sleep. Then he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set up on the earth, and its top reached to heaven; and there the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Jacob's Ladder.text: In the picture, we see Jacob who has fallen asleep and is having a dream. The artist has only shown Jacob himself and the very beginning of his dream. See the ladder? It goes all the way up to the sky. At the top of the ladder there's a bright light. Soon, angels will appear on the ladder. The angels will be going up and down the ladder, but we can't see that in the picture yet. Everything is still to come

Joseph and his brothers.verse: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age. Also he made him a tunic of many colors. But when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.
Joseph and his brothers.text: Here we see Joseph and his brothers. The brothers are talking to one another, some being occupied in thought.. Joseph is standing in the center of the painting. He is wearing special, colorful clothes. Joseph has his hands outstretched towards his brothers, as if he is ready to hug them all. But his brothers seem to be thinking about other things. What are Joseph's brothers thinking about? The painting seems to capture the moment when the brothers are starting to have evil thoughts.

Christ Leads Us from Sins to Virtues.id: Christ Leads Us from Sins to Virtues

Baby Moses.verse: So she called his name Moses, saying, “Because I drew him out of the water
Baby Moses.text: A basket woven from reeds drifts along the river. Can you see the tiny baby inside? The artist has painted the very plants that grow in Egypt, so we know exactly where this is happening. The mother, who is not shown in the painting, took desperate measures to save her child. She placed her baby in the basket and let it float away. The infant reaches out with his hands, as if seeking help from a lonely world.

Moses and the Burning Bush.verse: And the Angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush. So he looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed
Moses and the Burning Bush.text: In the painting, we see Moses. Do you see the bush painted in front of him? This is the same bush that is on fire but is not burning. Moses has one hand outstretched, and in this hand, Moses is holding a staff. He is covering his face with his other hand, as if trying to protect his eyes from the glow of the supernatural fire. I think he looks a little surprised. Maybe even a little scared. He is hearing a voice and trying to listen carefully to the words.

Israel passes thru the Red Sea.verse: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided.
Israel passes thru the Red Sea.text: In the painting, we see Moses. Moses is standing on the seabed. On one hand, Moses is holding a staff, and the other is raised up. He is calling to his people to follow him. In the painting, we also see the waves of the sea that have formed a wall of water and created a passage. The artist has painted a fish that is looking out from the wall of water. The fish cannot understand what is happening. Neither it nor the other fish have ever seen anything like this.

Christ is Our Shepherd and King.id: Christ is Our Shepherd and King

David the Anointed King.verse: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel arose and went to Ramah.
David the Anointed King.text: Who is this little boy? This is King David. He is wearing a white robe. Behind him stands a white sheep. The sheep is looking at us and David is kneeling and looking forward. In front of David, the artist has painted the prophet Samuel. Samuel is anointing David with oil. In this painting, Samuel is crowning the young David as king.

David the Psalmist.verse: Then David and all the house of Israel played music before the Lord on all kinds of instruments of fir wood, on harps, on stringed instruments, on tambourines, on sistrums, and on cymbals.
David the Psalmist.text: Painters usually depict kings on horseback, in battle armor. Often on the battlefield, sometimes in a luxurious palace with their subjects, or against the backdrop of a fortress. But in this painting, we see a king with a musical instrument — inspired and contemplative. His head is slightly bowed. His hands are touching the strings of the musical instrument. In the painting, we see a king who has gone through many trials. There were heroic deeds in his life and mistakes. We see a king who has acquired wisdom and is ready to share his wisdom with others.
